title: Quarterly governed rollout scheduler for hosted API model fleet
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a governed, repeatable scheduler to coordinate quarterly model rotations, canary windows, and capacity hedges for the Hosted API model fleet. The scheduler should: (1) expose commit windows aligned to capacity and SLA tiers, (2) orchestrate canary experiments with automated rollback triggers tied to eval and SLO signals, and (3) produce a publishable quarterly calendar for stakeholders and on-call teams.
background: Historically model rotations and endpoint updates have been scheduled in an ad-hoc fashion across PM, Eng, and SRE. This has caused overlap during high-traffic windows and inconsistent backout policies. The product team wants a standard quarterly rhythm that reduces risk, makes runbooks deterministic, and surfaces capacity needs to the Dedicated and Private teams in advance.
goals: Define a quarterly commit calendar with guarded windows per customer tier
Automate canary orchestration and tie rollbacks to observable thresholds (latency, error rate, quality regressions)
Provide a lightweight UI/CSV export for stakeholders and support rotations
Reduce failed rollouts by 60% relative to last two quarters
success_metrics: % of rollouts completed within scheduled windows: target 95%
Reduction in post-release incidents: -60% vs Q4 2024
Time to rollback (median): < 10 minutes when automated triggers fire
Number of manual holdovers due to capacity mismatch: <= 2 per quarter
milestones: 2025-02-28: Agree on gating signals and rollback thresholds
2025-03-12: MVP scheduler API spec (route + window model + dependencies)
2025-03-26: Canary automation prototype + integration test with runtime
2025-04-15: First scheduled rotation using the scheduler (pilot)
decisions: Chosen cadence: quarterly master calendar with weekly ephemeral slots for minor patches
Gating signals include: token latency p95, error rate, and model quality delta on a small eval set
Automated rollback will be enforced for severe SLA breaches; manual review for marginal quality deltas
Scheduler will emit a machine-readable calendar (iCal/CSV) and a human view in Console (low-fidelity for MVP)
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler API deployed to staging with documented endpoints and auth
Canary runbooks execute end-to-end in staging and trigger rollback on synthetic fault
Console page renders calendar and exposes ability to claim a slot
On-call runbook updated and linked from Console; SRE sign-off obtained
risks: Insufficient telemetry coverage for reliable gating signals (mitigation: add targeted tracing/metrics backlog)
Capacity estimation errors during seasonal traffic (mitigation: conservative hedges in first two quarters)
Cross-team coordination overhead—need early stakeholder alignment (mitigation: weekly sync through March)
Edge cases for model variants with different resource profiles (mitigation: model metadata tagging and per-model capacity hints)
notes: This ticket focuses on the scheduler and orchestration; rollout of feature flags + canary analysis logic will be tracked in ENG tickets
We will pilot with two non-critical endpoints first to validate rollback semantics
Consider later extension: automatic tagging of model variants and suggested quantization profiles based on past rollout telemetry
